Lemony white beans & spinach

Soft white beans, wilted spinach and a little lemon. Keep some bread nearby for the pan juices.

Prep
~5 min
Cooking
~10 min
Total
~15 min
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

Estimated to serve 2 people as a light meal with bread.

  • 1 tbsp olive oil
  • 2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
  • 240 g cooked white beans, drained and rinsed
    About 1 standard 15 oz / 425 g can, drained.
    Swap option

    Cooked butter beans, drained and rinsed (240 g)

    Texture: Larger and creamier in the centre — they hold their shape well.
    Flavor: Slightly richer and more buttery than cannellini.
    Adjust: Warm gently and check that the centres are hot. Avoid vigorous stirring.
    Prep: Warm gently and check that the centres are hot. Avoid vigorous stirring.

    Use the same drained weight; canned or already cooked beans only.

  • ⅓ cup (80 ml) water, plus a splash if needed
    Starting amount only. Pan size and evaporation affect how much you need.
  • ¼ tsp dried oregano
    Swap option

    Dried thyme (¼ tsp)

    Texture: No texture change — same dried herb format.
    Flavor: Earthier and woodsier than oregano, less Mediterranean.
    Adjust: Add with the beans and water. Taste before adding more.
    Prep: Add with the beans and water.

    Start with the same quantity; adjust to taste.

  • 3 cups (90 g) baby spinach, packed
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice, plus more to taste
  • Salt and black pepper, to taste
  • 2 slices bread, to serve

Bread may contain wheat and other allergens. Check all ingredient labels.

Advertisement

Method

You'll need
Wide skillet · Sieve · Knife and board · Wooden spoon · Measuring cup

Prepare

01

Get everything ready

Drain and rinse the beans. Slice the garlic, wash the spinach and measure the water and lemon juice.

Look for: Everything is ready before the garlic goes into the pan.

Extra tip

Drain the beans well. The measured water will give you more control over the sauce.

Cook

02

Gently warm the garlic

About 1 minute

Warm the olive oil in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the sliced garlic and stir until fragrant.

Look for: The garlic is pale and fragrant, with gentle sizzling.

Extra tip

Lower the heat if it colours quickly. Burnt garlic can make the sauce bitter.

03

Make the beans saucy

About 5 minutes

Add the white beans, measured water and oregano. Bring to a gentle simmer. Mash a spoonful of beans against the pan and stir it back into the liquid.

Look for: The beans are hot and the liquid lightly coats them.

Extra tip

Keep a gentle simmer. If it looks dry, add a splash of water; if watery, simmer briefly and check again.

04

Wilt the spinach

Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring each addition until it begins to wilt before adding more.

Look for: The leaves have softened and reduced in volume.

Extra tip

Add another splash of water only if the pan needs it.

Finish

05

Add lemon off the heat

Remove the skillet from the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Taste, season with salt and pepper, divide into portions and serve with the bread.

Look for: A lightly saucy pan of beans, with lemon adjusted to your taste.

Extra tip

Canned beans can already be salty, so taste before seasoning.

Why it works: Garlic kept pale adds fragrance without bitterness. Mashing a few beans thickens the liquid into a light sauce. Lemon goes in off the heat so its brightness stays lively.

Serve with

Serve warm with the bread listed in the ingredients. The stated yield is an estimate for a light meal, not a guarantee of appetite or nutritional adequacy.

One way to change it up

For a little crunch, add a few chopped radishes just before serving. This optional topping is not part of the base recipe.

Storage & Prep ahead

Drain the beans and measure the ingredients ahead if helpful. Keep prepared ingredients covered and refrigerated until cooking.

Keep at 40°F (4°C) or colder. Refrigerate within 2 hours of preparation, or within 1 hour above 90°F (32°C). Discard if left out longer. This development recipe does not yet have a tested refrigerated shelf life.
